story.title: Ebola Outbreak in DRC Surges as Death Toll Exceeds 2,500
story.summary: The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo is escalating rapidly, with the United Nations reporting that the death toll has surpassed 2,500. This outbreak is now the most severe in the country's recent history and is spreading at a significant rate, affecting an area larger than France. The World Health Organization is responding by supplying thousands of vaccine doses to help contain the virus.

event_overview.title: About Congo Ebola Outbreak
event_overview.subject: Congo Ebola Outbreak
event_overview.summary: The 2026 Congo Ebola outbreak is an ongoing epidemic of Ebola disease caused by Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD), first declared by the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda on May 15, 2026. It is centered in eastern DR Congo, where transmission expanded rapidly amid conflict, population movement, and limits on health-system access; WHO has classified the event as a Public Health Emergency of International Concern.

facts.label: Start and status
facts.value: The health ministries of DR Congo and Uganda declared outbreaks of Bundibugyo virus disease on May 15, 2026. As of August 21, 2026, the outbreak remained active in DR Congo; Uganda had declared its outbreak over on July 28 after 42 days without a new locally transmitted case.

facts.label: Disease agent
facts.value: The outbreak is caused by Bundibugyo virus, a species that causes Ebola disease. WHO reported that no licensed Bundibugyo-virus-specific vaccine or therapeutic was available, although candidate countermeasures were being developed and assessed.

facts.label: Location
facts.value: The epidemic began in Ituri Province and had spread to six DR Congo provinces by August 13: Ituri, North Kivu, South Kivu, Haut-Uélé, Tshopo, and an additional province reported in WHO's August risk assessment. Ituri remained the epicentre.

facts.label: Scale
facts.value: WHO's August 20 risk assessment reported 4,566 confirmed cases and 2,128 deaths in DR Congo as of August 13, 2026. Reported totals can change through delayed reporting, expanded testing, and reconciliation of earlier records.

facts.label: International framework and response
facts.value: On May 17, 2026, the WHO Director-General determined that the DR Congo–Uganda event constituted a Public Health Emergency of International Concern under the International Health Regulations. The response centers on surveillance, contact tracing, laboratory testing, infection prevention and control, clinical care, community engagement, and cross-border preparedness.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline highlights major developments from July 22 through August 11, 2026; it does not provide a complete case ledger, every local response measure, or all cross-border and international updates.

explore_lenses.label: Who is affected, and how does it spread?
explore_lenses.title: Six provinces are reporting cases
explore_lenses.summary: The outbreak has expanded beyond its initial focus in Ituri into six DRC provinces. Bundibugyo virus disease spreads through direct contact with the body fluids of symptomatic or deceased infected people, not through ordinary airborne exposure.

claims.text: As of August 12, 2026, WHO reported 4,665 confirmed cases and 2,184 deaths in DRC, across 54 health zones in Ituri, North Kivu, South Kivu, Haut-Uélé, Tshopo and Bas-Uélé.

CDC says people with Bundibugyo virus disease become contagious after symptoms begin; transmission occurs through direct contact with infected body fluids or contaminated objects, and it is not airborne.
WHO reported that the most recently affected province, Bas-Uélé, identified a case in a person with travel history to Haut-Uélé, illustrating how travel can carry infection into new areas.

explore_lenses.label: What do the reported tolls establish?
explore_lenses.title: The emergency is large, but counts are moving
explore_lenses.summary: WHO’s latest pre-story situation report confirms a rapidly expanding, high-fatality outbreak and describes it as the country’s largest recorded Ebola outbreak. But a rising reported total does not measure transmission alone, because case finding and testing have also expanded.

claims.text: WHO reported 4,665 confirmed DRC cases and 2,184 confirmed deaths as of August 12, 2026, a crude case-fatality ratio of 46.8%.
WHO said the outbreak had exceeded the 3,317 cases recorded in DRC’s 2018–2020 Ebola outbreak, making it the largest Ebola disease outbreak documented in the country by confirmed cases.

WHO said part of the increase reported between August 1 and August 12 reflected strengthened surveillance, laboratory testing and diagnostic capacity, while stating that most of the increase reflected geographic expansion of the outbreak.
UN Ebola coordinator Julien Harneis said on August 21 that more than 2,500 people had died and that half of those deaths occurred in the preceding 20 days.

explore_lenses.label: Will the vaccine doses contain this outbreak?
explore_lenses.title: Ervebo’s protection is unproven here
explore_lenses.summary: The outbreak is caused by Bundibugyo virus, whereas Ervebo is licensed for Zaire ebolavirus. WHO says evidence of cross-protection is too limited to support routine use, so vaccine doses alone should not be read as an established protective intervention.

claims.text: WHO states that there is no licensed vaccine for Bundibugyo virus disease and does not currently recommend Ervebo for Bundibugyo outbreaks because evidence that it protects against this virus is insufficient.

WHO’s emergency guidance says Ervebo should not be used programmatically against Bundibugyo virus outside controlled research settings; it recommends established measures such as surveillance, contact tracing, clinical care, infection prevention and community engagement.
WHO’s vaccine advisory group recommended prioritizing Ervebo for a Phase 3 research study during the outbreak while a Bundibugyo-specific candidate is not ready for evaluation.
CDC likewise says Ervebo is indicated for Zaire ebolavirus and is not expected to protect against Bundibugyo virus; supportive care and infection-control measures remain central.

story_report.summary: The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has expanded into the country’s largest documented Ebola outbreak by confirmed cases, with WHO reporting 4,665 cases and 2,184 deaths as of August 12. A UN Ebola coordinator said the death toll had risen above 2,500 by August 21, with half of those deaths occurring in the prior 20 days. The scale and geographic spread have intensified pressure on surveillance, care and infection-control operations, while the role of available vaccines remains constrained by the virus involved.

sections.heading: Outbreak expands across eastern provinces
sections.body: WHO said confirmed infections had been recorded in 54 health zones across Ituri, North Kivu, South Kivu, Haut-Uélé, Tshopo and Bas-Uélé. The outbreak has surpassed the 3,317 cases recorded during DRC’s 2018–2020 Ebola outbreak. WHO said strengthened surveillance, laboratory testing and diagnostics accounted for part of the increase between August 1 and 12, but that most of it reflected the outbreak’s geographic expansion.

sections.heading: Bundibugyo virus transmission risks
sections.body: CDC says people with Bundibugyo virus disease become contagious after symptoms start, and transmission occurs through direct contact with infected body fluids or contaminated objects rather than through the air. WHO reported that Bas-Uélé, the most recently affected province, identified a case in a person who had travelled from Haut-Uélé, demonstrating how travel can introduce infection into additional areas.

sections.heading: Vaccine strategy remains limited
sections.body: WHO says no licensed vaccine exists for Bundibugyo virus disease and does not recommend Ervebo for Bundibugyo outbreaks outside controlled research settings because evidence of protection is insufficient. Its emergency guidance emphasizes surveillance, contact tracing, clinical care, infection prevention and community engagement. WHO’s vaccine advisory group has recommended prioritizing Ervebo for a Phase 3 research study while a Bundibugyo-specific candidate is not ready for evaluation.

unresolved.text: The UN coordinator’s August 21 report of more than 2,500 deaths postdates WHO’s August 12 situation report, which recorded 2,184 confirmed deaths, so the newer toll cannot be independently confirmed from that WHO update.
Confirmed-case totals may be affected by changing surveillance and laboratory capacity as well as continuing transmission.

Whether Ervebo provides clinically meaningful cross-protection against Bundibugyo virus remains unresolved because available evidence is limited and does not provide a reliable effectiveness estimate.

related_stories.title: DR Congo to Receive 70,000 Doses of Ervebo Vaccine Amid Ebola Outbreak
related_stories.summary: The Democratic Republic of the Congo is set to receive 70,000 doses of the Ervebo vaccine to combat a surge in Ebola infections, particularly the Bundibugyo strain. The World Health Organization (WHO) has indicated that while it is uncertain if Ervebo will protect against this specific strain, preliminary laboratory and animal studies suggest it may offer some level of protection. A new trial will aim to determine the vaccine's efficacy in humans.

related_stories.title: Personalized mRNA Cancer Treatment Shows Promise Against Melanoma in Trial
related_stories.summary: Merck and Moderna announced that their personalized mRNA cancer treatment has successfully reduced melanoma tumor recurrence in a late-stage clinical trial. This marks a significant milestone in cancer treatment, as it is the first time an mRNA-based drug has shown positive results in such a large trial. Researchers are optimistic about the potential for this approach to be applied to other types of cancer in the future.

related_stories.summary: Spain has begun relocating hundreds of migrants from a makeshift camp on Ceuta's El Trampolín beach to temporary shelters. This action comes nearly three weeks after a mass border surge resulted in thousands of migrants living without adequate shelter in the North African enclave.

related_stories.title: New York Woman Charged with Terrorism for Alleged Capitol Bomb Plot
related_stories.summary: A 35-year-old woman has been charged with a terrorism offense for allegedly plotting to bomb the New York State Capitol. Jessica Bowie reportedly expressed a desire to destroy the Capitol buildings to an FBI informant, leading to her arrest in a sting operation. The charges are linked to her alleged support for the Islamic State (ISIS) group.
